notes: Reader A, part 1: sample_index 0 to 39 (rows from 16 PDF pages between 28 and 101; indices 0-27 are in the number-order section, 28-39 in the end-sorted section with the field at the left of the drawing). Each row was read from a 4x to 10x render of the original PDF page around the proposed box (PyMuPDF, pixels only) shown next to the supplied exact crop, and every sign was compared with the position-chart cards and, for hatched-patch and underline geometry, with PDF pages 20 and 21. Ink extents were measured in points from the exact crops (5 px per point) with a short script kept in my scratch folder. Units are listed in visual left-to-right order; no row in this part had an unnumbered continuation line, so each row has one physical line. Underline presence is treated as part of a sign's identity, as the chart does (for example 143 and 385). One unit has an empty strict set: in sample 3 the oval containing a slashed small oval has no underline, but the only chart card with that inner drawing (700) is underlined and card 160 shows a different inner mark; 700 and 160 are listed as shape-only candidates. Chart cards that look identical are kept together in one strict set: the tally-stroke cards 9/765, 10/766, 543/769 and 424/770 (they belong to different sign classes on chart page 20 but have the same drawing), and the labelled coincident cards 465/485/486 and 58/68. Narrow hatched patches (597/13 against 598/542) were assigned from spacing: an underline gives the cell directly (sample 10: patch at the left end of its underlined cell, card 13); otherwise a patch that ends about 2 pt before the next sign, or that starts about 2 pt after the previous cell ends, was given the right-edge or left-edge card respectively, and the other code stays in the shape-only list with uncertainty marked 'cell geometry' (samples 12, 17, 21, 25, 27, 29). I could not check this spacing model against any independent evidence, and the alignment of line ends does not separate the two cards. Samples 14 and 20 show two narrow hatched columns about 2.4-2.8 pt apart, the same size and spacing as the single two-column card 762 and also what two abutting narrow patches (598 then 597) would look like; I recorded one unit 762 and put the two-unit reading in count_alternatives. Sample 14 also has an isolated ring about 1 pt wide far to the left, which I counted as a speck (alternative count 3). Crop judgments: sample 30 is rejected because the first sign has four corner ticks and the two left ticks lie 0.7 to 1.5 pt outside the box, inside the field box. All other crops contain the whole drawing and underline and no neighbour or field ink; samples 22, 23, 24 and 36 have boxes 100-190 pt wide with the drawing in a small part of them, and the bottom two pixel rows of sample 21 carry the tips of the next line's ink (about 0.4 pt), which I did not treat as a reason to reject. Classification fields were transcribed with all five positions; the printed digit 1 often looks like a thin 'i' (for example '3i 42' is recorded as '31 42'), and a blank printed position is recorded as a space. Exposure: I listed the file names in the BLIND folder (no reader folders were present then) and opened only the files in files_opened; I saw no prediction, frame, pipeline output, other reader's work or text/OCR layer.
